blocks.note: Choose indicative for an asserted fact and subjunctive when the governing expression presents the event through desire, emotion, permission, expectation, or evaluation; exclude both judgment-dependent items.

Contrast the ordinary indicative after verbs of saying, thinking, and believing with the uncertainty introduced by negation or questioning; preserve the indicative after espérer and in clauses headed by interrogative si, and exclude all ambiguous or unmatched items.
Separate impersonal expressions that assert probability or evidence from those that mark doubt, possibility, necessity, or subjective evaluation; exclude all four judgment-dependent translations.

Apply the mood selected by purpose, concession, condition, result, and time conjunctions, including the avant que versus après que contrast; exclude all six alternatives that depend on register or interpretation.
Use the subjunctive when a superlative, seul, premier, dernier, or an equivalent expression makes a genuinely peerless claim, but retain the indicative for a factual member of an ordinary series.

Practise the subjunctive in coordinated hypothetical clauses, clause subjects, indefinite expressions, and hypothetical relative clauses; exclude all four items with competing literary and modern forms.

Choose devoir, pouvoir, savoir, falloir, or a tense construction from the intended modal meaning rather than translating the English modal word mechanically; exclude the one permission item with two accepted tenses.
Form unambiguous quantity, noun-focused, and third-person imperative exclamatives; exclude all four prompts whose printed key offers competing formulations.
